title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Conservation Workbench. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Conservation Workbench
options.lineage: museum conservation worksheets and accession records
options.thesis: A careful paper-and-ink desk where every claim is pinned to the bytes that support it.
options.viewport: A live PNG specimen sheet with its byte strip and Structure labels visible before the first click.
options.risk: Feels precious if the bytes recede; the sample must stay large and immediately usable.

raised.raise: Focus follows a single active span while the surrounding context quiets.
Structure labels use a strict index rhythm without retro phosphor color.
The page commits to one paper-and-ink environment instead of generic floating panels.

options.label: The Annotated Field Plate
options.thesis: The original file presented as a specimen whose parts can be named without losing the whole.
options.viewport: A specimen sheet with a large sample action and callouts that cross into the live tracer.
options.risk: The familiar field-guide metaphor can outrun the parser if labels are decorative instead of exact.

options.label: Event Display
options.thesis: Selection becomes one bright track through a quiet field of surrounding evidence.
options.viewport: A byte track arcs from signature to IHDR while exact offsets sit at the edge of the frame.
options.case: Competitive: it raises Selection clarity, but the conservation world identifies HexLens more clearly.
options.risk: Can look like a science demo instead of a readable inspection tool.

options.label: Strict Index Service
options.case: Declined: it keeps the index discipline, but loses product clarity when the novelty becomes the point.
options.kept: Strict, repeatable label rhythm for Structures and offsets.

options.label: Microfiche Reader
options.case: Declined: the environmental commitment is useful, but archival retrieval does not explain the product.
options.kept: A full field around the work, with no decorative dashboard chrome.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer dashboard with a file preview, tree, grid, and inspector.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional three-pane inspector with a standard marketing hero.
canonCard.risk: Easy to scan, but forgettable and visually interchangeable.
